title: Improving Qwen3.5-9B on τ³-Banking using PivotRL and fewer than 250 tasks
summary: Using fewer than 250 tasks from AfterQuery’s off-the-shelf data, on-policy distillation and PivotRL raised Qwen3.5-9B’s τ³-Banking pass@5 from 11.3% to 17.5%.
body_markdown:
We improved Qwen3.5-9B from **11.3% to 17.5% pass@5** on τ³-Banking using[AfterQuery’s off-the-shelf customer service tool use data](https://www.afterquery.com/contact) . We first distilled Qwen3.6-27B into the smaller model, then applied[PivotRL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21383) using teacher solutions for **only 50 tasks** .


## Methodology


### Stage 1 — Hybrid OPD


On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student using a teacher’s token-level feedback on the student’s own responses. We combined OPD with binary-reward RL.


The objective gradually shifted from pure reverse-KL distillation (β=1) toward binary-reward RL (β→0).


### Stage 2 — PivotRL


[PivotRL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21383) (Yi et al., 2026) is a turn-level RL method. It starts from existing SFT trajectories and treats each assistant turn as a possible training state. For each candidate turn, it samples several next actions from the frozen reference policy and scores them with a verifier. It keeps turns with mixed outcomes (some pass, some fail) and average reward below a difficulty threshold, discarding uniformly solved or uniformly failed turns. RL then samples fresh actions from the current policy at those retained “pivot” turns, using verifier rewards for locally valid actions rather than exact matches to the demonstration. On SWE-Bench, the paper reports accuracy comparable to end-to-end RL with about 4× fewer rollout turns.


We profiled **193 pivots from only 50 solved teacher trajectories** . A **functional-equivalence verifier** checked whether each sampled tool call did the same job as the teacher’s example. For lookups, it compared behavior in the replayed environment; for actions that changed data, it compared tool arguments after standardizing their format. This let PivotRL reward equivalent actions even when their tool-call text differed from the teacher’s.

## General capability check


We evaluated the base model and our selected checkpoint on six reasoning, knowledge, instruction-following, and coding benchmarks using NeMo Evaluator, with thinking enabled and the same evaluation harness.


None of the six benchmarks showed a statistically significant improvement or decline.
